components.name: Pad (button / chip / filter)
components.description: Flat hairline-bordered control; active state wears interconnect gold.
components.css: .ds-pad { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0.55rem 0.9rem; border: 1px solid rgba(242,239,230,0.14); border-radius: 3px; background: rgba(127,179,213,0.06); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: #b8c6d4; transition: border-color 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, background 0.18s ease; } .ds-pad:hover { border-color: #7fb3d5; color: #f2efe6; background: rgba(127,179,213,0.10); } .ds-pad:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c9a35c; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Active Pad
components.description: The active route/filter — gold border and text, the one active voice on the viewport.

components.name: Die Block (research / project cell)
components.description: Placed cell on the floorplan: cell code, title, description, topics, routed links.

components.css: .ds-block { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; padding: 1.25rem; border: 1px solid rgba(242,239,230,0.14); border-radius: 4px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(127,179,213,0.05) 0%, rgba(16,19,25,0) 100%); min-height: 100%; transition: border-color 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease; } .ds-block:hover { border-color: #7fb3d5; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-block-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; } .ds-cell-code { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #7fb3d5; border: 1px solid rgba(127,179,213,0.35); border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.1rem 0.375rem; } .ds-cell-name { font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; color: #f2efe6; text-align: right; } .ds-block-desc { font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.55; color: #b8c6d4; margin: 0; }

components.name: Stat Pad (pad ring)
components.description: A measured statistic on the pad ring: mono value with tabular numerals, tiny unit label.
components.css: .ds-stat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.15rem; padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem; border: 1px solid rgba(242,239,230,0.14); border-radius: 3px; background: rgba(16,19,25,0.72); } .ds-stat-value { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 1.05rem; font-weight: 500; color: #f2efe6; line-height: 1.1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-stat-unit { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8b9cac; }

components.name: Pin Link
components.description: Inline action with a drawn via dot; hover warms from metal blue to gold.
components.css: .ds-pin { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #7fb3d5; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.18s ease; } .ds-pin:hover { color: #c9a35c; } .ds-pin .ds-via { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; flex: none; }

narrative.overview: The SARCS website is drawn the way a chip designer reads a die: placed blocks, routed interconnect, mask-layer annotation, and a pad ring of measured statistics. Every page is a floorplan region of the same die; nothing pretends to be photography. The world is honest engineering graphics — the visitor sees the actual structures of the lab's research laid out as labeled cells with pins routed to their evidence, never stock imagery of someone else's hardware. The palette is silicon materials on deep substrate: oxide-white markings, metal-blue interconnects, and one warm interconnect-gold reserved for the active trace. The type system pairs a confident engineering grotesque (Archivo) with a measurement mono (JetBrains Mono) used only where an engineer would write data. Dark is not a mood choice; it is the substrate color of the mask-grid the world is drawn on, the screen a layout editor sits open on.
keyCharacteristics: Placed-cell composition: content sits in bordered, labeled regions like die blocks, not floating cards.
Routed interconnect: SVG traces with 45° miters and via dots draw from blocks toward their destinations; traces draw in once on load, then rest solid.
Pad-ring data: statistics and controls sit in flat, hairline-bordered pads — never elevated, never glowing.
Construction honesty: every annotation is real and readable; no decorative chrome, no fake hardware photos, no glass.
One authored motion moment: the pin-trace draw-in. Everything else is state feedback.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No element casts a shadow. Depth comes from hairline borders, tonal fills, and the grid — never from elevation. A zero-offset glow is decoration and is banned.

rules.name: The Gold Rarity Rule
rules.body: Interconnect gold marks the active thing only. Two gold accents on one viewport means neither is active.

rules.name: The Oxide Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders and dividers are oxide white at low alpha (14% at rest, 30% at emphasis) — never gray, never black-on-black.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No label sits above a heading. The heading carries its own weight; a die-label may sit beside or below it as annotation, never above it as a teaser.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measurement Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where a number, code, date, or label is being read — stats, edge codes, tags, navigation. Body copy and long prose are always Archivo.

dos: Do draw every figure as a flat, hairline-bordered cell on the grid.
Do reserve interconnect gold for the active element — one per viewport.
Do set statistics in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do keep one authored motion moment (the trace draw-in) and nothing more.
Do theme browser surfaces — selection, scrollbar, focus rings — from the palette.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass, backdrop-blur, glow, or drop shadows anywhere.
Don't place a label above a heading — the heading carries itself.
Don't use monospace for body prose or as a tech costume.
Don't ship stock photography of hardware the lab does not own; schematic truth beats fake realism.
Don't let any element overflow the viewport horizontally — grids collapse via CSS media queries, never inline grid definitions.
